intent: Changed: sensor row moved forward from y = 0.04 m to y = 0.06 m, as the Integrator requested. Kept the widened x = -0.024 to +0.024 m spacing, 12 mm sensors, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body and mass 0.8 kg, so this race isolates the forward offset. Expected result: s-bend and slalom max_error falls below 0.06 m more often, with slalom and s-bend progress up, while the oval finish rate holds near 0.5 or more. If the oval finish rate falls well below 0.5, the forward offset costs more than it gains, and the iteration 1 geometry is the base to keep. I am not considering any sensor-size, track or mass change.
learning: Compare directly with iteration 1 (y = 0.04 m, score 324.07), since only the sensor row's y position differs. The simulator is deterministic, so any change is attributable to the offset. If s-bend or slalom max_error drops below 0.06 and the oval finish rate holds, the forward row is the new base. If the oval finish rate drops, the controller's gain is tied to the y = 0.04 m row, and the Integrator should judge whether the controller can be retuned for the new row.
rationale: Iteration 7 held the iteration 1 geometry, and iteration 6 reproduced its score exactly (324.07, oval finish 0.70). The simulator is therefore deterministic for a fixed design, so single-race comparisons are reliable. Every geometry change tested so far has lowered the score: 16 mm sensors (159.26), wheel_track 0.10 m (175.19), mass 0.6 kg (247.82) and mass 0.7 kg (185.49). The remaining gap is on the s-bend and slalom, where max_error sits at about 0.064 m, just above the 0.06 m off-track limit. Body width cannot raise that limit within its range, so it is not a lever. The Integrator's only untested geometry idea is a forward sensor offset to y = 0.06 m with the widened row kept. I am taking that single change now. It tests whether moving the sensing row forward gives the controller earlier warning on bends, which is the one mechanism left that could reduce s-bend and slalom max_error. The base the Integrator tuned against is unchanged except for this one variable: 12 mm sensors, x = -0.024 to +0.024 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.16 m, mass 0.8 kg. Risk: the controller was tuned to the y = 0.04 m row, so the forward row may change the signal gain and cost oval finishes. If the oval finish rate falls well below 0.5, I will return to the iteration 1 geometry as the final base.
